newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Avesta Sheffield says optimistic for price rises.
newsitem.headline: Avesta Sheffield says optimistic for price rises.

text.p: Anglo-Swedish steel group Avesta Sheffield said on Friday that it continued to be optimistic that stainless steel prices would rise after the summer holiday period.

"The market for stainless steel continues to grow by four to five percent a year and I continue to be optimistic for price rises after the holiday period," the company's managing director Stuart Pettifor said in a statement.
Pettifor said that after a year of disappointment, he was convinced that the company would return to profitability.
"The bit challenge for management is to ensure that the company's cost base is reduced at the same time as production increases and there is growth in the market," he said.
He said investing in new equipment in Avesta and Nyby in Sweden should boost capacity usage.
"The group will have a very strong production base and this will give a platform for growth through value added products and for strong profitability," Pettifor said.
Avesta Sheffield, which is 51 percent owned by British Steel, posted a loss of 124 million crowns for the year to March 31, 1997, against a profit of 3.60 billion crowns a year earlier.
